title: Finite-presentation data at an inverse limit

proof.text: *Base change bookkeeping.* Let $i\le i'\le i''$ and let $V$ be an $X_i$-scheme. Since $f_{i'i}\circ f_{i''i'}=f_{i''i}$ and $f_{i'i}\circ f_{i'}=f_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], transitivity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] gives canonical isomorphisms $(V_{i'})_{i''}\cong V_{i''}$ over $X_{i''}$ and $(V_{i'})_X\cong V_X$ over $X$, compatible with each other and with base change of $X_i$-morphisms; base change is a functor: $(\psi\circ\chi)_{i'}=\psi_{i'}\circ\chi_{i'}$, $(\psi\circ\chi)_X=\psi_X\circ\chi_X$, $(\mathrm{id})_{i'}=\mathrm{id}$. Likewise, for an $X_i$-morphism $g:V\to W$ and $i'\ge i$, $V_{i'}\cong W_{i'}\times_WV$ with $g_{i'}$ the projection. If $V\to X_i$ is etale of finite presentation, then so are $V_{i'}\to X_{i'}$ and $V_X\to X$ (etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3)), and the scheme $V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2) because $X_i$ is. Finally, any $X_i$-morphism between two $X_i$-schemes etale over $X_i$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3).

proof.text: *Objects (assertion 1).* Let $U\to X$ be etale of finite presentation. By [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1) (Stacks 01ZM (1): $U\cong U'_{i,X}$ as schemes over $X$) there are $i\in I$, a morphism of finite presentation $U'_i\to X_i$ and an $X$-isomorphism $\beta:(U'_i)_X\to U$. The structure morphism $(U'_i)_X\to X$ is the composite of $\beta$, an isomorphism and hence an open immersion, which is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), with the etale $U\to X$; so it is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] to the system $(X_j)$, the index $0:=i$, $S_0=Y_0:=X_i$, $X_0:=U'_i$ and $f_0$ the structure morphism of $U'_i$: $S_0$ and $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by hypothesis, $X_0$ by step 1, $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation, and its base change to $X$ is $(U'_i)_X\to X_i\times_{X_i}X=X$, etale. Hence there is $i'\ge i$ with $(U'_i)_{i'}\to X_{i'}$ etale. Put $U_{i'}=(U'_i)_{i'}$: it is etale of finite presentation over $X_{i'}$ (finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3)), and $(U_{i'})_X\cong(U'_i)_X\cong U$ over $X$ by step 1 and $\beta$.

*Morphisms and equalities (assertions 2 and 3).* $U_i$ and $V_i$ are of finite presentation over $X_i$. For 2, [thm-pd-spreading-out] (2) gives $i'\ge i$ and a morphism $\psi_{i'}:(U_i)_{i'}\to(V_i)_{i'}$ whose base change to $X$ is $\psi$; as in Stacks 01ZM (2), and in the Lean declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_pullback_hom_of_isLimit of that node, $\psi$ is a morphism over $X$ and $\psi_{i'}$ one over $X_{i'}$ (the base change to $X$ is only defined for these). For 3, [thm-pd-spreading-out] (3) gives $i'\ge i$ with $\psi_{i'}=\chi_{i'}$.

*Finite diagrams (assertion 4).* For each $a\in A$ step 2 gives a stage $i_a$, an $X_{i_a}$-scheme etale of finite presentation and an $X$-isomorphism to $U^a$. As $A$ is finite and $I$ directed, choose $i\ge i_a$ for all $a$ ($i$ arbitrary if $A=\emptyset$) and base change everything to $X_i$; by step 1 this gives $X_i$-schemes $U^a_i$ etale of finite presentation and $X$-isomorphisms $\alpha_a:(U^a_i)_X\to U^a$. For $e\in E$ the $X$-morphism $\varphi_e=\alpha_{t(e)}^{-1}\circ\psi_e\circ\alpha_{s(e)}:(U^{s(e)}_i)_X\to(U^{t(e)}_i)_X$ descends by step 3 (assertion 2) to an $X_{i_e}$-morphism at some stage $i_e\ge i$; choose $i'\ge i_e$ for all $e\in E$ and replace $i$ by $i'$, the $U^a_i$ by their base changes, the $\alpha_a$ by their composites with the isomorphisms of step 1, and the descended morphisms by their base changes $\psi_{e,i}$; then $(\psi_{e,i})_X=\varphi_e$, i.e. $\alpha_{t(e)}\circ(\psi_{e,i})_X=\psi_e\circ\alpha_{s(e)}$. For a relation $c=c'$ of $R$ with chains $e_1,\dots,e_m$ and $e'_1,\dots,e'_{m'}$ from $a$ to $a'$, let $\gamma=\psi_{e_m,i}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{e_1,i}$ and $\gamma'$ likewise (identity for an empty chain). By functoriality of base change (step 1) and telescoping of the $\alpha$'s, $\gamma_X=\alpha_{a'}^{-1}\circ c\circ\alpha_a=\alpha_{a'}^{-1}\circ c'\circ\alpha_a=\gamma'_X$, so by step 3 (assertion 3) $\gamma_{i_r}=\gamma'_{i_r}$ at some $i_r\ge i$. Taking a common $i''\ge i_r$ for the finitely many $r\in R$ and base changing once more (base change preserves the relations, the etale and finite-presentation properties and the compatibility with the $\alpha$'s, by step 1) gives a descended diagram at stage $i''$. The same reasons show that the base change of a descended diagram at stage $i$ to any $i'\ge i$ is one at stage $i'$.

proof.text: *Coverings (assertion 5), descent of surjectivity.* Each $\psi_{e,i}$ ($e\in B$) is an $X_i$-morphism between $X_i$-schemes etale over $X_i$, hence etale (step 1), in particular locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $V=\coprod_{e\in B}U^{s(e)}_i$ with coprojections $\iota_e$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and $g:V\to U^b_i$ the morphism with $g\circ\iota_e=\psi_{e,i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-lfp-qcqs] (2) $g$ is locally of finite presentation, and by its part (1) $V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, each $U^{s(e)}_i$ being so by step 1; so is $U^b_i$. The base change $g_X:V_X\to(U^b_i)_X$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]: for $y\in(U^b_i)_X$ the point $\alpha_b(y)$ lies in the image of some $\psi_e$ ($e\in B$), because the family is jointly surjective [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]: $\alpha_b(y)=\psi_e(u)$; then $z=\alpha_{s(e)}^{-1}(u)$ satisfies $(\psi_{e,i})_X(z)=\alpha_b^{-1}\psi_e\alpha_{s(e)}(z)=y$, and $(\psi_{e,i})_X=g_X\circ(\iota_e)_X$ by functoriality (step 1), so $y\in g_X(V_X)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] to the system $(X_j)$, $0:=i$, $S_0:=X_i$, $X_0:=V$, $Y_0:=U^b_i$ and $f_0:=g$ (a morphism over $X_i$ between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, locally of finite presentation, with surjective base change to $X$): there is $i_1\ge i$ with $g_{i_1}$ surjective. For $i'\ge i_1$, $g_{i'}$ is by step 1 the base change of $g_{i_1}$ along $(U^b_i)_{i'}\to(U^b_i)_{i_1}$, hence surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].

source.place: Lemma 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069), applied to the morphism from the finite coproduct

proof.text: *Coverings (assertion 5), conclusion.* Let $i'\ge i_1$. The coprojections $\iota_e:U^{s(e)}_i\to V$ are open immersions covering $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], hence a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] applied to the projection $V_{i'}\to V$, the projections $V_{i'}\times_VU^{s(e)}_i\to V_{i'}$ are jointly surjective; by step 1 $V_{i'}\times_VU^{s(e)}_i\cong(U^{s(e)}_i)_{i'}$ with these projections becoming $(\iota_e)_{i'}$. Since $g_{i'}$ is surjective (step 5) and $(\psi_{e,i})_{i'}=g_{i'}\circ(\iota_e)_{i'}$ (step 1), every point of $(U^b_i)_{i'}$ lies in the image of some $(\psi_{e,i})_{i'}$, $e\in B$. Each $(\psi_{e,i})_{i'}$ is an $X_{i'}$-morphism between objects of $(X_{i'})_{\Et}$ (step 1), etale by step 1. So $\{(\psi_{e,i})_{i'}\}_{e\in B}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms, a covering in $(X_{i'})_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].
